{{Short description|Two inequalities in mathematical analysis}}
In [[mathematical analysis]], '''Agmon's inequalities''', named after [[Shmuel Agmon]],<ref>Lemma 13.2, in: Agmon, Shmuel,  ''Lectures on Elliptic Boundary Value Problems'',  AMS Chelsea Publishing, Providence, RI, 2010. {{ISBN|978-0-8218-4910-1}}.</ref>  consist of two closely related [[interpolation inequality|interpolation inequalities]] between the [[Lp space|Lebesgue space]] <math>L^\infty</math> and the [[Sobolev space]]s <math>H^s</math>.  It is useful in the study of [[partial differential equation]]s.

Let <math>u\in H^2(\Omega)\cap H^1_0(\Omega)</math> where <math>\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^3</math>{{vague|date=May 2015}}.  Then Agmon's inequalities in 3D state that there exists a constant <math>C</math> such that

: <math>\displaystyle \|u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\leq C \|u\|_{H^1(\Omega)}^{1/2} \|u\|_{H^2(\Omega)}^{1/2},</math>

and

: <math>\displaystyle \|u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\leq C \|u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^{1/4} \|u\|_{H^2(\Omega)}^{3/4}.</math>

In 2D, the first inequality still holds, but not the second: let <math>u\in H^2(\Omega)\cap H^1_0(\Omega)</math> where <math>\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^2</math>.  Then Agmon's inequality in 2D states that there exists a constant <math>C</math> such that

: <math>\displaystyle \|u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\leq C \|u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^{1/2} \|u\|_{H^2(\Omega)}^{1/2}.</math>

For the <math>n</math>-dimensional case, choose <math>s_1</math> and <math>s_2</math> such that <math>s_1< \tfrac{n}{2} < s_2</math>.  Then, if <math>0< \theta < 1</math> and <math>\tfrac{n}{2} = \theta s_1 + (1-\theta)s_2</math>, the following inequality holds for any <math>u\in H^{s_2}(\Omega)</math>

: <math>\displaystyle \|u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\leq C \|u\|_{H^{s_1}(\Omega)}^{\theta} \|u\|_{H^{s_2}(\Omega)}^{1-\theta}</math>
